1.q: וַ֠⁠יִּשְׁלַח חִירָ֨ם מֶֽלֶךְ־צ֤וֹר אֶת־עֲבָדָי⁠ו֙ אֶל־שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה כִּ֣י שָׁמַ֔ע כִּ֥י אֹת֛⁠וֹ מָשְׁח֥וּ לְ⁠מֶ֖לֶךְ תַּ֣חַת אָבִ֑י⁠הוּ כִּ֣י אֹהֵ֗ב הָיָ֥ה חִירָ֛ם לְ⁠דָוִ֖ד כָּל־הַ⁠יָּמִֽים
1.note: The author is reintroducing **Hiram** as a participant in the story. He first appeared in 2 Samuel 5:11. If your language has its own way of reintroducing participants, you could use it here in your translation. Alternate translation: [And Hiram, king of Tyre, who had been a friend to David all of the days, sent his servants to Solomon when he heard that they had anointed him as king in place of his father]

1.q: וַ֠⁠יִּשְׁלַח חִירָ֨ם מֶֽלֶךְ־צ֤וֹר אֶת־עֲבָדָי⁠ו֙ אֶל־שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה כִּ֣י שָׁמַ֔ע כִּ֥י אֹת֛⁠וֹ מָשְׁח֥וּ לְ⁠מֶ֖לֶךְ תַּ֣חַת אָבִ֑י⁠הוּ
1.note: The author is describing one event, Hiram sending his servants to Solomon, before describing another event that preceded it, the Israelites anointing Solomon as king. If it would be helpful in your language, you may wish to relate these events in the order in which they happened, as in the UST. Alternate translation: [And when Hiram, king of Tyre, heard that they had anointed Solomon as king in place of his father, he sent his servants to him]

Here the author is using the pronoun **they** in a general sense, not to refer to specific people. Use an expression for this that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [he had been anointed]

The author is using the term **days** to mean time, since time is made up of days. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [all the time] or [continually]

2.note: The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language, here and in 5:8. Alternate translation: [And Solomon sent messengers]

Make sure that it is clear in your translation that this is not what Solomon said to his own messengers. It is what he told them to say to Hiram on his behalf. Alternate translation: [to say to him on his behalf]

3.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 2:5. Alternate translation: [You know quite well]

It might seem that this expression contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [that David my father was not able]
See how you translated the similar expression in [3:1](ta:03). Alternate translation: [a temple]
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:2. Alternate translation: [for the worship of Yahweh] or [for the reputation of Yahweh]

Here, **from the face of** is a common expression of the culture that means “because of” or “on account of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [on account of]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **warfare**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the wars they fought against him on all sides]
The pronoun **they** refers to David’s enemies. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [his enemies surrounded him]

3.q: עַ֤ד תֵּת־יְהוָה֙ אֹתָ֔⁠ם תַּ֖חַת כַּפּ֥וֹת רגל⁠ו
3.note: Solomon is speaking as if David had performed a symbolic action against his enemies. In this culture, victorious soldiers would make defeated enemies lie face down on the ground, and they would then step on their necks to demonstrate their complete triumph (as in Joshua 10:24, for example). If it would be helpful to your readers, you could express the meaning plainly in your translation. Alternate translation: [until Yahweh enabled him to defeat them all completely]

In this verse, the word **foot** is singular in form, but it refers to both of David’s feet. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “foot.” Alternate translation: [his feet]

4.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 1:12.

5.note: Solomon is using a common expression of his culture, **behold me**, to indicate that he is about to do something. If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. If you have already translated the book of 2 Samuel, see how you translated the similar expression in 2 Samuel 12:11. Alternate translation: [And I am currently intending]
In this context, the term **saying** means “intending.” The idea is that Solomon has been **saying** to himself that he will do this. Alternate translation: [And behold me, intending]
See how you translated the similar expression in 5:3. Alternate translation: [for the worship of Yahweh] or [for the reputation of Yahweh]

5.q: לֵ⁠אמֹ֔ר בִּנְ⁠ךָ֗ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֶתֵּ֤ן תַּחְתֶּ֨י⁠ךָ֙ עַל־כִּסְאֶ֔⁠ךָ הֽוּא־יִבְנֶ֥ה הַ⁠בַּ֖יִת לִ⁠שְׁמִֽ⁠י
5.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [telling him that his son, whom he would put in David’s place on his throne, would build the house for his name]
See how you translated the similar expression in 2:24. Alternate translation: [whom I will make succeed you as king] or [whom I will make rule the Israelites after you]
See how you translated the similar expression “you, you swore” in 1:17. Alternate translation: [he is the one who will build]

6.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 1:12.

The word translated as **command** is an imperative, but it communicates a polite request rather than a command. Use a form in your language that communicates a polite request. It may be helpful to add an expression such as “please” to make this clear. Alternate translation: [please command]
Here Solomon is using the pronoun **they** to refer to Hiram’s workers. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and may your workers cut]
Here the word **For** introduces not a reason but an explanation. Alternate translation: [After all,]
See how you translated the similar expression in 2:5. Alternate translation: [You know quite well]

7.note: Here, **words** represents what Solomon said by using words. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [what Solomon had sent the messengers to tell him]
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:48. Alternate translation: [May people bless Yahweh] or [May people praise Yahweh]

Here, Hiram is speaking of Solomon as if he were positioned **over** the people. He is indicating Solomon’s role as their ruler. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to rule]

8.note: See the discussion in the introduction to 1 Kings of this use of the term “heard.” Alternate translation: [I agree to do what you sent messengers to ask me to do]

Hiram is stating the pronoun **I** separately, even though the verb translated as **I will do** already includes this meaning. He is doing that because he is making an agreement with Solomon. See how you translated the similar expression “I, I will speak” in 2:18. Alternate translation: [I agree to do]
See how you translated the similar expression in 2:26. Alternate translation: [I agree to command my servants to do]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **desire**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [everything you want] or [everything that you have asked]

9.note: Hiram is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [And my servants will bring down the trees that they cut]
See how you translated the similar expression “I, I will do” in 5:8. Alternate translation: [and for my part, I will set rafts]

Hiram is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and float them to the place]

Hiram is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [that you send messengers to indicate to me] or [that you designate to me]
See how you translated the similar expression **I, I will set** earlier in this verse. Alternate translation: [And for your part, you will lift]

Hiram is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [And for your part, you will have your servants lift the logs out of the sea and bring them to Jerusalem]
See how you translated the similar expression “I, I will do all of your desire” in 5:8. Alternate translation: [And I would like you to agree to do what I desire]
See how you translated the similar expression in 4:22. Alternate translation: [by providing food for my royal household]

10.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **desire**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [as many trees of cedar and trees of cypress as he desired]

11.q: וּ⁠שְׁלֹמֹה֩ נָתַ֨ן לְ⁠חִירָ֜ם עֶשְׂרִים֩ אֶ֨לֶף כֹּ֤ר חִטִּים֙ מַכֹּ֣לֶת לְ⁠בֵית֔⁠וֹ וְ⁠עֶשְׂרִ֥ים כֹּ֖ר שֶׁ֣מֶן כָּתִ֑ית
11.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about the **oil** together with the information about the **wheat**. Alternate translation: [And Solomon gave to Hiram 20,000 cors of wheat and 20 cors of beaten oil as food for his house]

11.q: עֶשְׂרִים֩ אֶ֨לֶף כֹּ֤ר חִטִּים֙ & וְ⁠עֶשְׂרִ֥ים כֹּ֖ר שֶׁ֣מֶן כָּתִ֑ית
11.note: Each of these **cors** was equivalent to 220 liters or nearly 60 gallons. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could express this in terms of modern measurements, either in the text or in a footnote. The UST models one way to do that.

Here the author is using the term **house** to represent the people who lived and worked in Hiram’s royal palace. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [for his royal household]

The author is using **year by year** as a common expression of his culture to mean “every year” or “each year.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from year to year] or [every year]

12.q: וַ⁠יהוָ֗ה נָתַ֤ן חָכְמָה֙ לִ⁠שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה כַּ⁠אֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּר־ל֑⁠וֹ וַ⁠יְהִ֣י שָׁלֹ֗ם בֵּ֤ין חִירָם֙ וּ⁠בֵ֣ין שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וַ⁠יִּכְרְת֥וּ בְרִ֖ית שְׁנֵי⁠הֶֽם
12.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about Yahweh giving wisdom to Solomon last in this verse, since it seems to apply to the description in the following verses of how Solomon administered this project. Alternate translation: [And peace was between Hiram and between Solomon, and the two of them cut a covenant. And Yahweh gave wisdom to Solomon, just as he had spoken to him.]

12.q: וַ⁠יְהִ֣י שָׁלֹ֗ם בֵּ֤ין חִירָם֙ וּ⁠בֵ֣ין שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וַ⁠יִּכְרְת֥וּ בְרִ֖ית שְׁנֵי⁠הֶֽם
12.note: The author is describing one event, peace being between Hiram and Solomon, before describing another event that preceded it, the two of them making a covenant. If it would be helpful your language, you may wish to relate these events in the order in which they happened, as in the UST. Alternate translation: [And Hiram and Solomon cut a covenant, and peace was between the two of them]

The author is using **cut a covenant** as a common expression of his culture to mean “made a covenant.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. If you have already translated the book of 1 Samuel, see how you translated the similar expression in 1 Samuel 11:1. Alternate translation: [and the two of them made a covenant] or [and Hiram and Solomon made a covenant]

13.note: In this context, the author is not saying **brought up** to mean that Solomon made these men travel to a higher elevation, Lebanon, although they did that. Instead, he is using **brought up forced labor** as a common expression of his culture to mean that Solomon forced these men to do this work. If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And King Solomon raised a levy] or [And King Solomon called up a work force]
See how you translated the similar expression in 4:6.
Here, **Israel** represents the people of Israel. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the people of Israel]

14.note: In this verse, the word **house** is singular in form, but it refers to all the workers’ homes as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “house.” Alternate translation: [two months in their houses]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and then they were two months in their houses]
See how you translated the similar expression in 4:4. Alternate translation: [And Adoniram was in charge of the forced labor]

15.q: וַ⁠יְהִ֧י לִ⁠שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה שִׁבְעִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף נֹשֵׂ֣א סַבָּ֑ל וּ⁠שְׁמֹנִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף חֹצֵ֥ב
15.note: In this verse, the words **carrier of a burden** and **quarrier** are singular in form, but they refer to all the workers as groups. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of these terms. Alternate translation: [And there were to Solomon 70,000 burden carriers and 80,000 quarriers]

15.q: שִׁבְעִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף נֹשֵׂ֣א סַבָּ֑ל וּ⁠שְׁמֹנִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף חֹצֵ֥ב בָּ⁠הָֽר
15.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about the quarriers before the information about the carriers, since the quarriers would first dig out the stones and the carriers would then drag them away. Alternate translation: [80,000 quarriers in the hill country and 70,000 burden carriers]

Here the author uses a general expression, **a carrier of a burden**, for someone who would transport goods by picking them up and carrying them. However, the huge blocks of stone that the other workers were cutting for the temple were far too heavy for anyone to carry. Even a large group of men could not have picked them up and carried them. So use a term here in your translation that indicates more generally that these men transported the stone blocks. (They probably did this by mounting the stones on sledges and pulling the sledges over a series of round wooden logs that teams of men would move from the rear to the front in succession.) Alternate translation: [70,000 transporters] or [70,000 haulers of stone]

A **quarrier** is a person who cuts stone out of rock formations. If your readers would not be familiar with what a quarrier is, you could use a more general term or explain it in a footnote. Alternate translation: [a stone cutter] or [a person who cut stone]

16.q: לְ֠⁠בַד מִ⁠שָּׂרֵ֨י הַ⁠נִּצָּבִ֤ים לִ⁠שְׁלֹמֹה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־הַ⁠מְּלָאכָ֔ה
16.note: The author is using the possessive form to describe **commanders** who were **deputies of Solomon**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [apart from the deputies of Solomon who were commanders over the work]

17.note: The author is explaining in more detail what the quarriers did whom he describes in 5:15. You may be able to use a form of a verb in your language that makes clear that the author is not describing something that Solomon **commanded** after he put these 80,000 men to work. Alternate translation: [As the king had commanded, the quarriers removed]

By **valuable stones**, the author means stones that had been carefully chosen and skillfully prepared for use in the temple foundation. He does not necessarily mean that they were precious stones such as marble or porphyry. The surviving portions of Solomon’s temple indicate that it was built of limestone blocks. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [high-quality limestone blocks]

The author is using the possessive form to describe **stones** that were characterized by **hewing**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [stones that they cut into shape]

18.note: The author is using the term **builders** to refer to all of the men whose labor contributed to the building of the temple. He does not mean that they were all involved in constructing the temple itself. As the context shows, most of them were involved in collecting and transporting the materials. You may wish to use a more general term in your translation. Alternate translation: [Solomon’s workers and Hiram’s workers]

The workers from the city of Gebal were experts in squaring stones for buildings. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and the men he brought in from the city of Gebal, who were experts in squaring stones]
